text:
Gabe Perreault is playing on the Rangers' top line, beside Mika Zibanejad and Alexis Lafrenière, and he's starting to look like he belongs there. He has six goals in 19 games, two of them in his last three, and he opened the scoring in Seattle on Nov. 7. Nothing about it looks like a heater: his goals sit right on his expected goals (5.65), and the Rangers take 54.6% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five.

The 23rd pick in 2023 was a Boston College scorer who our league translation had at about 55 points over 82 NHL games in his last college season, and his game is built on speed into space: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 60% of his shots coming off the rush last season, in a small sample of eight games. At 0.47 points a game, he's ahead of the median for forwards picked 18th to 28th since 2005 (0.37 in their first full season). Our projection lands around 22 goals and 45 points, and his power-play role (three points so far) is the thing that could push it higher.
